issues.body:

Three quiet ratchet runs of the before-state and three of the after-state, interleaved in one session, recorded in the milestone's Records. It measures; it changes no code. The exit is perigrin's relative one ("Relative and ≤ 5 (Recommended)"): the after-reading's median `speed-ratio-aggregate-longlived` below the before-reading's minimum, and at or below 5.

## Prerequisites

- STAGEKEYS (01a20950-3f3c): its merge commit on `pu` is the before-state.

**The two states.** Before: STAGEKEYS's merge commit on `pu`. After: `pu` once every other issue of this milestone has merged. Check out each in its own worktree (never in the shared checkout), built once before the session.

**The session.** Six runs, interleaved B A B A B A, in one session on one machine. Quiet is a 1-minute load at or below the core count: read `/proc/loadavg` and `nproc` before each run and wait for quiet. If a quiet session cannot be had, take the reading anyway, record the load, and report to perigrin: that is a Stop for him to rule on.

**One measurement** is one ratchet run's printed value of a key, which is the protocol's own median of three. Do not re-median or discard runs.

**What it records.** For `speed-ratio-aggregate-longlived` and the three stage keys (`speed-stage-precedence-aggregate-longlived`, `speed-stage-resolve-aggregate-longlived`, `speed-stage-readings-aggregate-longlived`), before and after: median, min and max over the three runs. Other `speed-stage-*` keys may be added.

**Where.** One Records bullet in the milestone body, one line, beginning `- <date> verdict reading:`, naming each key with its before and after median, min and max, the two states as `before-commit <sha>` and `after-commit <sha>` (these exact tokens), each run's load, cores and kernel, their excluded files (or "excluded: none"), and ending with `exit: met` or `exit: not met` and with `precedence-stage stop: fired` or `precedence-stage stop: not fired` (these exact lower-case tokens; it fires when the after median of `speed-stage-precedence-aggregate-longlived` is not below the before minimum). ## Steps

## Rules

These come from the milestone's Process rules, which bind every issue, worker, runner and reviewer:
- Its own branch off `pu` and its own pull request. Rebase onto `pu`, never merge `pu` in. Merge with a merge commit, never squash. Never push to `pu`, `main` or `master`.

issues.body:
**Reconstructed** from the session transcript, text exact; original id `01a20e1e-ca39-733d-823f-418c3f0fc3b7`, delivered as perigrin/pvm#639 (merge 4c5a153b4).

The findings in full are in the round-2 reports under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f57559af-f6d7-50b1-b4d1-2c3218e70a25/scratchpad/review-w3/: r2-fresh.md (F1–F3), r2-coverage.md (C6–C9), r2-quality.md (Q10) and r2-ponytail.md (P9). Read all four.

## Context

- paths: `internal/chart/` only
- **F1 (the code fix).** In `(*Precedence).stateFree`, the shift-side loop records a key's verdict (spine top, rule-position item, terminal) only from states that shift that terminal. A state that holds the same key but does not shift the terminal, because it is reached through a nullable prefix, has no conflict in bison: there the shift is allowed. The guard never sees that "allowed", so the tables keep the other state's "forbidden" as a guess and `NewPrecedence` raises no error.
  - **The toy:** `S ::= TA V | TB V | TA K F | TA K2; V ::= TC P; K ::= TC X %prec HIGH; K2 ::= TC X F TH; P ::= X Y; Y ::= E F; E ::= ; X ::= TX`, with `%left F` below `%left HIGH`.
  - **What goes wrong on it:** `Constrain` refuses `TB TC TX F`, while bison 3.8.2 and `ConstrainReference` accept it.
  - **The fix:** iterate over the terminals of FIRST(rhs[j]) (and rhs[j] itself), and record "allowed" where the state does not shift the terminal. After the fix, the guard errors on the toy instead of guessing.
  - **Reach today:** perly.y has 0 such keys, so its tables are unchanged.
- **Production and the referee.** Production is `(*Forest).Constrain`. The referee, `ConstrainReference`, is frozen: never edit its body.

## Steps

- [ ] **Docs first** (`docs(chart): …`, docs-only):
  - **F2:** state precisely what the guard proves, including that a state holding the key without shifting the terminal counts as allowed.
  - **F3 and C6:** reword the "Keep" bullet and "The parser states are bison's" bullet so they describe production's rule (the shift is checked only where the state shifts the terminal) and not the referee's defect.
  - **C7:** the sentence classing any future differential failure "of that shape" as the reference's defect goes past the Q1 ruling. Say instead that the pinned toy is the one divergence ruled the referee's, and that any other failing §3.4 check is a Stop reported to perigrin (decision §5).
  - **C8 and Q10:** scope "No perly.y forest reaches it", in both the README and `ConstrainReference`'s doc comment, to the evidence. Round 2 instrumented generation and found 0 defect sites on perly.y's grammar, and found no in-tree or perl.git file that diverges; name that observation and the revision it was made on (423da4dd7).
  - **C9:** the differential bullet's "two copies of one forest" is wrong for `comparePrecedence`, which copies once and runs the reference on the original. Say what each harness does.
- [ ] **F1:** apply the fix in `stateFree`. Add the toy as a case of `TestPrecedenceGenerationGuard`, named so its subtest is `TestPrecedenceGenerationGuard/nullable_prefix`. The case asserts that generation fails with an error naming the item, the terminal and the spine-top item.
  - Show the case red on the unfixed loop.
  - Show perly.y still generating: the existing perly case.
- [ ] **P9:** the cmd/ratchet stage-pin test's comment says its hand-built toy is the known-divergence toy, but the copy differs: it has no `Z ::= HIGH`. Make the comment say what the copy is.
- [ ] Run make test, then open the PR.

## Rules

issues.title: Check perly.y for the nullable-shift precedence limit and pin it
issues.body:
**Reconstructed** from the session transcript, text exact; original id `01a20e50-2026-75e5-b880-1943691b4f05`, delivered as perigrin/pvm#640 (merge fd43942c0).

**Handle:** `REVIEWFIX3`. This issue comes from REVIEWFIX2's gate finding G1. It is scoped by perigrin's ruling "Check perly.y, then pin (Recommended)", recorded in Records.

**The limit.** Both judgements refuse a sentence that bison accepts: production `(*Forest).Constrain` and the referee `ConstrainReference`. Because they agree, the differentials cannot see it.

The toy:

```
S ::= TA V | TA K2
V ::= TC P
K2 ::= TC X F TH
P ::= X Y
Y ::= E F
E ::= %prec HIGH
X ::= TX
```

`%left F` is below `%left HIGH`. bison 3.8.2 accepts `TA TC TX F` by reducing E.

Why the judgements refuse it: the state shifts F through K2, and E's own reduction beats that shift. So the key (`V: TC . P`, `P: X . Y`, F) is recorded as forbidden, even though bison builds the derivation through E. The limit also falsifies the README's "the one bison builds is kept" for this shape.

Decision §6 puts changing what precedence decides out of V1's scope. So the fix is a follow-up, and this issue only checks and pins.

## Context

- paths: `internal/chart/` only
- Never edit `ConstrainReference`'s body. Production's behaviour must not change.

## Steps

- [ ] **Check perly.y first.** Write a test, `TestPrecedenceNullableShiftLimitAbsent`, that walks perly.y's automaton at generation time and counts the keys of this shape.
  - The shape is a shift key (spine top, rule-position item, terminal f) recorded as forbidden where the state shifts f, while a nullable symbol at the item's dot can derive ε and then reach f. That includes nullable chains of any length, not only a single empty rule.
  - The test asserts the count is 0 on perly.y. It also asserts the count is at least 1 on the toy above, so the counter is shown to see the shape.
  - Construct both the passing and the failing case. A counter that never fires proves nothing.
  - **If perly.y's count is not 0, stop and report it. That is a milestone Stop for perigrin.**
- [ ] **Pin the limit.**
  - Add `TestPrecedenceNullableShiftKnownLimit`. On the toy, it asserts that `Constrain` and `ConstrainReference` both refuse `TA TC TX F`, and that bison's recorded answer is accept. Cite the bison version and the state.
  - At the shift-side loop in `stateFree`, add a comment in the form `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
  - Add a README line to "The precedence constraint" stating the limit. Correct "the one bison builds is kept" to scope it.
  - Docs first.
- [ ] Run make test, then open the PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Positive Scenarios
- [ ] perly.y has no key of the limit's shape, and the counter sees the toy's (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/forest/ -run "^TestPrecedenceNullableShiftLimitAbsent\$" -count=1 -v 2>&1) || { printf "%s\n" "$out" | tail -20; exit 1; }; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q "^--- PASS: TestPrecedenceNullableShiftLimitAbsent "'`)
- [ ] the known limit is pinned against bison's answer (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/forest/ -run "^TestPrecedenceNullableShiftKnownLimit\$" -count=1 -v 2>&1) || { printf "%s\n" "$out" | tail -20; exit 1; }; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q "^--- PASS: TestPrecedenceNullableShiftKnownLimit "'`)
- [ ] the limit is stated where it lives: a shortcut comment in precedence.go and the README's precedence section name it (`sh -c 'grep -q "shortcut:" internal/chart/forest/precedence.go || { echo "no shortcut comment"; exit 1; }; awk "/^## The precedence constraint/ { s = 1; next } s && /^## / { s = 0 } s" internal/chart/README.md | grep -q "TestPrecedenceNullableShiftKnownLimit" || { echo "the README does not name the known limit"; exit 1; }'`)
- [ ] guard: `make test` (`sh -c 'T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test; s=$?; git checkout -q -- test/e2e/.perl-version; exit $s'`)

### Negative Scenarios
- [ ] the referee's body is unchanged since the delivery (`sh -c 'f(){ git show "$1:internal/chart/forest/precedence.go" | awk "/^func \\(f \\*Forest\\) ConstrainReference\\(/ { p = 1 } p { print } p && /^}/ { exit }"; }; a=$(f 2a29efd2e); test -n "$a" || exit 1; [ "$a" = "$(f HEAD)" ] || { echo "ConstrainReference body changed"; exit 1; }'`)
